qa_pair.question: Inspect the catalog of Action1 action templates and identify the one whose required parameters include a field that controls which exit codes count as success on Windows. Provide the template id verbatim.
The Action1 platform exposes a dedicated action template for executing arbitrary shell scripts on macOS endpoints, separate from the Windows PowerShell template. What is its template id?
Look up the run_script action template via the MCP server. Among its parameters, which one accepts the literal string "Bash" as one of its allowed values? Provide the parameter name verbatim.
Look up the run_script action template via the MCP server. Among its parameters, the `platform` parameter takes a literal string value for macOS endpoints. What is that value (case-sensitive)?
Among Action1's built-in action templates, identify the one whose template id is used for rebooting endpoints. Provide the literal template id.

The MCP server's `action1_get_endpoint` tool returns a `platform` field whose value is one of a fixed set of strings. Provide the four possible values comma-separated, lowercase, alphabetically sorted (no spaces between commas).

The MCP server's `action1_get_automation_output` tool filters status-marker lines out of the raw script output it receives from Action1. Three specific status keywords identify these lines. Provide them comma-separated, alphabetically sorted (no spaces).

Use the `action1_get_action_template` tool to inspect the `deploy_update` template. Within its `reboot_options` parameter group, the `auto_reboot` value can be set to one of three literal strings. Provide them comma-separated, alphabetically sorted (no spaces).

Inspect the run_powershell template's `success_exit_codes` parameter. The MCP server's curated wrapper defaults this parameter to a single-character literal string when the caller omits it. Provide that literal value.
Use action1_list_action_templates and identify the action template that allows uninstalling software on an endpoint. Provide its template id verbatim.
The MCP server exposes a tool that removes a single endpoint from an endpoint group (the counterpart to adding one). Provide its tool name verbatim.
